To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the plastidic isopre-noid biosynthesis in two related tomato species is affected by drought stress and the tolerant one has higher expression and activity in some of the genes and metabolites of the pathway.
the isoprenoid metabolism is a key component in the response to water deficit, and that the synthesis of some of these metabolites, as α-tocopherols, could be a key component in drought tolerance.
the isoprenoid pathway in tomato is modulated by drought stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the physiological and molecular mechanisms involved in plant tolerance to drought stress.
the analysis of the physiological and molecular responses to drought of the isoprenoid pathway in two related species, and the identification of the genes involved in these responses.
the analysis of the isoprenoid pathway under drought stress and its possible contribution to the adaptation to water deficit of the S. chilene species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
drought stress in S. chilenese and S. lycopsericum affects the isoprenoid metabolism in a different way.

, under drought stress, S. chilene is able to maintain its photosynthetic capacity by means of a more efficient use of water, and by increasing the synthesis of α-tocopherols, which would protect its membranes against oxidative damage.

the plastidic isopentenyl diphosphate pathway is involved in the response of plants to abiotic stress, and that the differences in the expression of the genes encoding the enzymes of this pathway between S. chilenses and S. lycoperisicum plants may explain, in part, the differences in the response to drought stress between the two tomato species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plastidic isopreoid pathway is functional in both species, and that it is involved in plant response and adaptation to abiotic stress.
the plastidic isoprene and α-tocopherols biosynthetic pathways play an important role in drought tolerance of S. chilese.

the differences between both species in the response to water stress are related to the activity of the isoprenoid pathway in the chloroplasts, and that the expression of some of its genes, such as HPT1, is a key factor in the response of S. chilenese to drought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plastidic isopernoid pathway plays a relevant role in the drought response of S. chilese and that the HPT1 gene is a potential candidate for engineering drought tolerance in tomato.

the analysis of isoprenoid metabolism in tomato plants under water deficit conditions is useful to identify the molecular mechanisms involved in the response of this species to abiotic stress, and to identify new genes involved in the response to drought.
